homepage.what_is_p1: Windrose (also known as Windrose: Pirate Survival RPG) is a pirate-themed survival adventure developed by Kraken Express and co-published with Pocketpair Publishing. Released into Early Access on April 14, 2026, the game blends classic survival crafting with soulslite combat — a lighter take on Soulslike mechanics that rewards timing, positioning, and stamina management without being overly punishing.
homepage.what_is_p2: The game takes place across a procedurally generated open-sea archipelago where players can explore islands, gather resources, build bases, craft hundreds of items, and sail between locations on ships they construct themselves. Windrose supports solo play and co-op multiplayer for up to 10 players, making it ideal for both lone adventurers and organized crews.
homepage.core_systems_desc: Windrose combines five interconnected systems that define its gameplay loop. Each system feeds into the others — resources fuel crafting, crafting equips your character, and better gear opens new bosses and islands.
homepage.feature_crafting_desc: Over 950 items across multiple tiers of crafting stations. From Workbench tools to Weaponsmith weapons — build your base anywhere with a free-form system.
homepage.feature_combat_desc: Dodge-roll, perfect block, and stamina management form the core. Boss encounters feature multi-phase attack patterns that demand practice.
homepage.feature_sailing_desc: Construct and customize ships from Sloop to Frigate class. Navigate dynamic wind systems, manage cargo, and engage in naval combat.
homepage.feature_resource_desc: Mine copper, iron, clay, and gunpowder from cave deposits and surface nodes. Each resource has specific island biomes where it spawns.
homepage.feature_progression_desc: Level up by clearing POIs and completing quests. Allocate talent points across Toughguy, Swashbuckler, and Mariner trees with free respecs.

progression.intro: The fastest reliable Windrose start is not to build a huge base immediately. Build only what unlocks tools, smelting, healing, and your first ship, then move toward the next island chain with enough supplies to recover from mistakes.

progression.short_answer_html: To progress quickly in Windrose, craft a Stone Pickaxe, mine copper and clay, build a Charcoal Kiln and Smelting Furnace, smelt Copper Ingots, then craft Copper tools before pushing toward your first ship and Foothills.

faqs.q: Should I build a permanent base early?
faqs.a: No. A small camp near resources is more efficient until you understand the island layout and unlock better tools.

faqs.q: What should I carry before leaving the first island?
faqs.a: Bring bandages, food, repair materials, copper tools, and enough wood or stone to rebuild basic stations.

resource.intro: Use this planner to decide what to farm before you craft a station or leave an island. The most common player mistake is collecting random materials without knowing which tool gate they are trying to open.
table_rows: Iron tools, Lv2 recipes, advanced bags
Smuggler stashes, pirate camps, later crafting
resource.farming_order_p: Wood, stone, and plant fiber come first. Clay and copper unlock smelting. Copper tools bridge into iron. Iron and sulfur push the late resource chain for stronger tools, backpacks, and ammunition.

faqs.q: What resource should I farm first?
faqs.a: Wood and stone are first, but copper and clay are the first real progression resources.

faqs.q: Where should I farm gunpowder early?
faqs.a: Use smuggler stashes and pirate camps before you can craft gunpowder from sulfur and ash.

ship_selector.intro: Pick your Windrose ship by job, not by size. The Sloop is easiest to maneuver, the Brigantine is the safest all-rounder, and the Frigate is a commitment to firepower and crew coordination.
table_rows: Solo scouting, fast travel between islands
Heavy naval battles and late fights
ship_selector.quick_rec_html: For most players, build toward the Brigantine. It has enough control for exploration and enough strength for fights without forcing the slow handling of a Frigate.

faqs.q: What is the best solo ship?
faqs.a: The Sloop is the easiest solo ship because speed and turning matter more when you do not have a full crew.

faqs.q: What is the best general ship?
faqs.a: The Brigantine is the best default recommendation because it balances speed, firepower, and survival.

mining.intro: Mining is the core of mid-game progression. This guide covers the most efficient routes for Copper, Iron, and Sulfur to minimize travel time and maximize yield.
mining.s1_html: Before leaving the starter island, locate the two cave icons. Bring a Stone Pickaxe and at least 3 torches. Clear the caves entirely, which should yield about 60-80 Poor Copper Ore. Smelt this immediately to craft your Copper Pickaxe and Weaponsmith.
mining.s2_html: Once you reach the Foothills, Iron Ore becomes your bottleneck. The best route starts at the Southern coast fast travel bell, heading north along the cliff base. You will encounter 4-5 iron deposits. Always bring a Brigantine or larger ship to store the heavy ore, as inventory weight will limit you quickly.
mining.s3_html: Sulfur spawns near volcanic vents in the Foothills and Cursed Swamps. Combine Sulfur with Ash (from burning wood) at the Alchemy Table to craft Gunpowder. A single run through the Eastern Swamp vents yields enough for ~100 bullets.

faqs.q: What is the best pickaxe?
faqs.a: The Iron Pickaxe is the most efficient for all mid-game ores.

faqs.q: Do ores respawn?
faqs.a: Yes, ore nodes typically respawn after 2 in-game days.

boss_progression.intro: Bosses in Windrose are major progression gates. You cannot access certain islands or craft advanced ship parts without defeating them. Here is the optimal progression path and strategy for each.
boss_progression.s1_html: Level 5-6. The first major roadblock. Richards uses slow, heavy saber swings. Strategy: Wait for his 3-hit combo to finish, then heavy attack. Do not get greedy. A simple Rapier is highly effective here due to its fast attack speed.
boss_progression.s2_html: Level 8-10. Hands uses firearms and calls reinforcements. Strategy: Use the pillars in the arena to block his musket shots. Focus on clearing his crew first, then chip away at his health. Bring at least 10 Healing Potions.
boss_progression.s3_html: Level 12-15. A magic-based boss with massive AoE attacks. Strategy: Mobility is key. Use a Sloop to reach her island quickly if you die. Equip armor with high elemental resistance. Her attacks inflict Poison, so bring Antidotes crafted at the Alchemy Table.

faqs.q: Can I skip bosses?
faqs.a: No, story bosses drop key items needed for crafting the Brigantine and Frigate.

faqs.q: Do bosses scale in co-op?
faqs.a: Yes, bosses gain increased health and damage for each additional player in the server.

builds.intro: Your build determines your combat effectiveness. Because respecs are free, you can experiment, but these three early-game builds will carry you safely to the late game.
builds.s1_html:
Weapons: Rapier or Saber + Pistol
Talents: Focus on the 'Duelist' tree. Maximize dodge i-frames and critical hit chance.
Playstyle: Fast-paced hit-and-run. Use the Pistol to stagger enemies, then dash in for critical melee strikes. Excellent for solo players.
builds.s2_html:
Weapons: Heavy Club or Boarding Axe + Blunderbuss
Talents: Focus on the 'Toughguy' tree. Maximize HP, Stamina, and Perfect Block window.
Playstyle: Stand your ground. Perfect block enemy attacks to stagger them, then deliver massive heavy attacks. Best for co-op frontlining.
builds.s3_html:
Weapons: Musket + Dual Pistols
Talents: Focus on the 'Sharpshooter' tree. Maximize ranged damage and ammo crafting efficiency.
Playstyle: Keep your distance. This build requires heavy farming for Gunpowder and Lead, but safely deletes enemies before they reach you.

faqs.q: Can I respec my talents?
faqs.a: Yes, respecs are completely free at any time from the character menu.

faqs.q: What is the best solo build?
faqs.a: The Swashbuckler (Agility/Crit) provides the mobility needed to survive multiple enemies alone.

ship_building.intro: Naval combat is one of Windrose's most unique systems. This guide covers everything from upgrading your starter Sloop to commanding a Frigate fleet in late-game naval battles.
ship_building.s1_html: You receive a free Sloop after completing the starter island quest chain. The Sloop is fast and agile but fragile — it has only 2 cannon slots and low hull HP. Use it primarily for scouting islands and avoiding fights. If enemies engage, outrun them rather than trading shots.
ship_building.s2_html: The Brigantine requires defeating the first boss (Thomas Richards) to unlock its blueprint. Materials: 80 Wood + 40 Copper Nails + 20 Iron Ingots + 10 Rope + Sail Fabric. The Brigantine has 4 cannon slots, significantly more HP, and can carry a full crew of 4 players comfortably. This is where naval combat becomes viable.
ship_building.s3_html:
• Wind Direction — Your ship speed depends on wind angle. Sailing with the wind gives maximum speed; sailing against it slows you to a crawl. Use the wind indicator on your compass.
  • Cannon Types — Round shot for hull damage, grape shot for crew damage, chain shot for mast damage. Always carry all three.
  • Boarding — When an enemy ship is disabled (mast destroyed), pull alongside and press F to board. Boarding is the fastest way to loot pirate ships.
  • Repair Kits — Craft Ship Repair Kits before any naval engagement. A single hole below the waterline will slowly sink your ship.
ship_building.s4_html: The Frigate is a floating fortress with 8 cannon slots, massive HP, and cargo space. It requires defeating Israel Hands and gathering Foothills-tier materials. Only build a Frigate if you have a co-op crew of 3+ — solo players cannot operate all cannons effectively.

faqs.q: Which ship should I build first?
faqs.a: Always upgrade to the Brigantine first. It is the best balance of firepower and maneuverability.

faqs.q: Can my ship be destroyed permanently?
faqs.a: No. If your ship sinks, it respawns at the nearest dock, but you lose all cargo stored on board.

sailing.intro: Windrose's world is massive — over 30 procedurally generated islands across three biomes. Knowing how to navigate efficiently saves hours of gameplay time.
sailing.s1_html: Wind direction changes every in-game day. The compass HUD shows the current wind direction with a small arrow. Sailing with the wind (downwind) gives maximum speed. Sailing at 90° to the wind (beam reach) gives about 70% speed. Sailing directly into the wind (upwind) reduces you to 30% speed. Plan your routes based on wind direction to avoid painfully slow crossings.
sailing.s2_html: Right-click the map to place custom markers. Always check "Show on minimap" so markers appear on your HUD. Mark these immediately: home bases, resource nodes, cave entrances, boss arenas, and dangerous areas. There is no limit to the number of markers.
sailing.s3_html: Craft Fast Travel Bells (10 Copper Ingot + 3 Rope) and place them strategically. Recommended locations: your main base, Foothills landing, Cursed Swamps entrance, and near each boss arena. You can teleport between any two bells instantly, but your ship does not teleport with you — plan accordingly.
sailing.s4_html:
• Coastal Jungle — Starter biome. Low-level enemies, abundant wood and copper. Safe for new players.
  • Foothills — Mid-game. Iron ore, sulfur, tougher enemies. Requires copper-tier gear minimum.
  • Cursed Swamps — Late game. Poisonous enemies, rare materials, the High Priestess boss. Bring antidotes and iron-tier gear.

faqs.q: Does my ship teleport with fast travel?
faqs.a: No. Your ship stays where you left it. You must sail it manually to your destination.

faqs.q: How do I find new islands?
faqs.a: Sail toward unexplored areas on your map. New islands appear as fog lifts when you get close enough.

crafting_progression.intro: Crafting in Windrose follows a strict tier system. Understanding which stations unlock which recipes — and in what order — prevents wasted resources and backtracking.
crafting_progression.s1_html: Progression follows this order: Hand Crafting → Workbench Lv1 → Charcoal Kiln + Smelting Furnace → Workbench Lv2 → Weaponsmith → Armor Workshop → Workbench Lv3. Each tier unlocks recipes that feed into the next, creating a clear upgrade path.
crafting_progression.s3_html:
• Don't skip the Charcoal Kiln. Many players try to smelt ore without charcoal. The kiln is mandatory.
  • Build stations under roofs. The Weaponsmith and Armor Workshop require a roof to be placed.
  • Recipes are material-gated. Some recipes only appear after you pick up a specific material for the first time.

faqs.q: Why can't I see a recipe?
faqs.a: Most recipes are hidden until you collect the primary material. Pick up new resources to unlock recipes automatically.

faqs.q: What is the most important crafting station?
faqs.a: The Smelting Furnace is the most important mid-game station because it converts raw ore into usable ingots.

coop.intro: Windrose shines in co-op. This guide covers how to set up multiplayer, what to expect with different group sizes, and strategies for efficient crew play.
coop.s1_html: From the main menu, select "Host Game" to create a session, or "Join Game" to browse public sessions. You can also join friends directly through Steam. Private servers require a password set by the host.
coop.s2_html:
In an ideal crew of 4:

  • Captain (1) — Steers the ship, manages navigation, calls targets during naval combat.
  • Gunner (1-2) — Operates cannons during naval battles. Switches between ammo types as needed.
  • Scout/Gatherer (1) — Explores ahead, gathers resources, marks dangers on the map.
  • Boarder (1) — Specializes in melee combat for ship boarding and dungeon clearing.
coop.s3_html: Progression is tied to the world save, not individual characters. All players share the same world state, quest progress, and base. However, character levels and talents are per-character. This means a new player joining a late-game world will be under-leveled — they should grind POIs and quests to catch up.
coop.s4_html: For persistent worlds that run 24/7, set up a dedicated server using SteamCMD (App ID: 4129620). See our Dedicated Server Guide for step-by-step setup. Dedicated servers prevent progress loss when the host disconnects.

faqs.q: Can I play Windrose solo?
faqs.a: Yes. The game is fully playable solo, though some bosses and naval combat are significantly easier with a crew.

faqs.q: Do items transfer between worlds?
faqs.a: No. Characters keep their level and talents, but inventory and equipment are tied to each world save.
